title: Finite-type reduction for tensor products
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-pc-field-extension] and let $R$, $S$ be $k$-algebras; call a ring reduced if it has no nonzero nilpotent elements, and a $k$-subalgebra finitely generated if it is generated as a $k$-algebra by finitely many elements. (1) If $R\otimes_kS$ is not reduced, then there are finitely generated $k$-subalgebras $R'\subset R$ and $S'\subset S$ such that $R'\otimes_kS'$ is not reduced. (2) If $R\otimes_kS$ contains a nonzero zero-divisor, then there are finitely generated $k$-subalgebras $R'\subset R$ and $S'\subset S$ such that $R'\otimes_kS'$ contains a nonzero zero-divisor.

proof.text: Let I_R (respectively I_S) be the directed poset of finitely generated k-subalgebras of R (respectively S), ordered by inclusion. It is directed because the k-subalgebra generated by two members is again finitely generated and contains both, and its union is R (respectively S), since every element belongs to the subalgebra it generates. Thus R and S are filtered colimits of these subalgebras. The elementwise representative property for filtered colimits of commutative algebras is [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise].

Suppose R tensor_k S has a nonzero nilpotent z, with z^n=0. Regard S as fixed and R as the filtered colimit from Step 1. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-tensor-elementwise], z is the image of some z_i in R_i tensor_k S, and the zero element z_i^n has image zero in R tensor_k S, so after increasing i it becomes zero. Now regard this enlarged R_i as fixed and S as the filtered colimit from Step 1; applying the same representative and eventual-zero assertions to z_i and z_i^n gives finitely generated subalgebras R' subset R and S' subset S for which the corresponding element z' in R' tensor_k S' is nonzero and satisfies (z')^n=0. Hence R' tensor_k S' is not reduced.

Suppose x and y are nonzero elements of R tensor_k S with xy=0. Apply the representative part of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-tensor-elementwise] to x and y and pass to a common larger finitely generated R_i so that both are represented in R_i tensor_k S. Apply its eventual-zero part to the representative of xy to enlarge i until the product is zero there. The representatives of x and y remain nonzero, because their images in R tensor_k S are nonzero. Finally apply the same two assertions with R_i fixed and S expressed as the filtered colimit of its finitely generated subalgebras, passing to one common S' for both representatives and their zero product. The resulting finitely generated R' subset R and S' subset S therefore have nonzero x' and y' with x'y'=0, so R' tensor_k S' contains a nonzero zero-divisor.

lean.statement: theorem tensor_finite_type_limit (k : Type u) [Field k] (R : Type v) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] (S : Type w) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] : (¬ IsReduced (R ⊗[k] S) → ∃ (R' : Subalgebra k R) (S' : Subalgebra k S), Algebra.FiniteType k R' ∧ Algebra.FiniteType k S' ∧ ¬ IsReduced (R' ⊗[k] S')) ∧ ((∃ x y : R ⊗[k] S, x ≠ 0 ∧ y ≠ 0 ∧ x * y = 0) → ∃ (R' : Subalgebra k R) (S' : Subalgebra k S), Algebra.FiniteType k R' ∧ Algebra.FiniteType k S' ∧ ∃ x y : R' ⊗[k] S', x ≠ 0 ∧ y ≠ 0 ∧ x * y = 0)
